title: Countable cohomology DG modules are telescopes of compact objects
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Compact means that $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}(Q,N_\alpha)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q,\bigoplus_\alpha N_\alpha)$ is bijective for every small family [def-pc-compact-object]. Assume $H^i(A)$ is countable for every integer $i$. Let $M\in D(A,d)$ have countable $H^i(M)$ for every integer $i$. There exist compact objects $Q_m\in D(A,d)$, maps $u_m:Q_m\to Q_{m+1}$ and compatible maps $b_m:Q_m\to M$, with $b_{m+1}u_m=b_m$, and a distinguished triangle
$$\bigoplus_mQ_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\bigoplus_mQ_m\xrightarrow{b}M\longrightarrow(\bigoplus_mQ_m)[1],\qquad s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}u_m,\quad b\iota_m=b_m.$$
The coproducts are indexed by $\mathbf N$ in the fixed ambient universe and homotopy colimit has the meaning of [def-kun-truncations].

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dg-countable-subalgebra], choose a countable DG subalgebra $A_0\subseteq A$ inducing all cohomology isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-qis-restriction-equivalence] to the inclusion $A_0\to A$. Restriction $R:D(A,d)\to D(A_0,d)$ leaves the underlying cochain complex unchanged and commutes strictly with sums, shifts and the cone $N\oplus K[1]$ of a module map $K\to N$, so it is exact; that node says it is an equivalence of triangulated categories with exact quasi-inverse and left adjoint $L=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_0}A:D(A_0,d)\to D(A,d)$, whose unit and counit $\epsilon:LR\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ are isomorphisms commuting with the shift comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, proof (2) to (1), paragraph 'By Lemma lemma-qis-equivalence the restriction map D(A,d) -> D(A',d) is an equivalence'; Tag 09S6.

proof.text: Choose a DG module representative $N$ of $R(M)$. Since restriction does not change the underlying complex, $H^i(N)=H^i(M)$ is countable. The algebra $A_0$ is countable as a total graded set. Thus [lem-sfb-dg-countable-semi-free-resolution] gives $q:P\to N$, a quasi-isomorphism, and a countable homogeneous graded basis $\{x_j\}_{j\in J}$ with natural-number heights $h(j)$ such that every $d(x_j)$ has finite support in strictly smaller heights.

For any finite set $S$ of basis labels, close it under the basis supports of $d(x_j)$. This closure is finite: induct on the maximum height of $S$; all added labels have smaller height, each support is finite, and height zero adds nothing. Its span is a DG submodule, since $d(x_ja)=d(x_j)a+(-1)^{|x_j|}x_jd(a)$ stays in that span. Choose finite sets $S_m$ increasing with union $J$ (also when $J$ is finite or empty). Let $T_0$ be the closure of $S_0$ and $T_{m+1}$ the closure of $T_m\cup S_{m+1}$. Then $C_m=\bigoplus_{j\in T_m}x_jA_0$ are nested DG submodules with union $P$. Intersecting with the height filtration gives each $C_m$ a finite filtration whose quotients are finite direct sums of shifts of $A_0$: the quotient basis generators have zero differential modulo smaller heights.

By [lem-sfb-dg-finite-cell-compact], the images $E_m$ of $C_m$ in $D(A_0,d)$ are compact. The module colimit of their inclusion sequence is $P$: every finite-support element is in some $C_m$. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle] to these actual DG inclusions. It gives the telescope triangle with third object $P$ and legs the inclusions. Compose its third-object isomorphism with $q:P\xrightarrow{\sim}N\simeq R(M)$ in the derived category, and denote the resulting legs by $c_m:E_m\to R(M)$. Thus $c_{m+1}v_m=c_m$, and their coproduct is the second arrow of a distinguished telescope triangle with third object $R(M)$.

Both equivalences preserve every small coproduct: for a family $Z_a$ in $D(A_0,d)$ and $Y$ in $D(A,d)$, the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(L(\bigoplus_aZ_a),Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_aZ_a,R(Y))\cong\prod_a\operatorname{Hom}(L(Z_a),Y)$ give the coproduct universal property with the images of its coprojections. Interchange $L,R$ for the other direction. The same Hom bijections and the defining compactness bijection [def-pc-compact-object] show that $Q_m=L(E_m)$ is compact: for any family $Y_a$, compute its Hom into $\bigoplus_aY_a$ using $R(\bigoplus_aY_a)\cong\bigoplus_aR(Y_a)$ and compactness of $E_m$. All index families remain small in the fixed ambient universe.

Apply [lem-kun-functor-preserves-hocolim] to the exact, countable-coproduct-preserving $L$ and the triangle of step 4. The required countable coproducts in both DG derived categories exist by [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle]. Define $u_m=L(v_m)$ and $b_m=\epsilon_M L(c_m):Q_m\to M$. Then $b_{m+1}u_m=\epsilon_M L(c_{m+1}v_m)=b_m$. Under the coproduct comparison $\bigoplus_mL(E_m)\simeq L(\bigoplus_mE_m)$, the image first arrow is $1-s$, since on its $m$-th coprojection it is the identity minus the next coprojection composed with $L(v_m)$. Identify $LR(M)$ with $M$ by $\epsilon_M$. The second arrow now restricts to $b_m$ on every coprojection, and the resulting distinguished triangle is exactly the asserted one, with homotopy-colimit convention [def-kun-truncations].
